recipes.name: Chef John's Macaroni and Cheese
ingredients_raw: 3 cups shredded sharp Cheddar cheese, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook elbow macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Melt 1/4 cup butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. When butter starts to foam and bubble, stir in flour; cook on medium heat until flour begins to turn pale yellow, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add thyme, cayenne, and white pepper; cook and stir another minute, then whisk in 1 cup milk until smooth. Pour in remaining milk and whisk again. Bring sauce just to a simmer.
Stir in salt, Worcestershire sauce, and nutmeg. Simmer, whisking often, on medium-low heat until thickened, about 8 minutes.
Turn heat off, then add 2 1/4 cups Cheddar cheese; stir until melted and combined. Mix in Dijon mustard.
Transfer macaroni into a 8x8-inch casserole dish, then pour in cheese sauce; stir to thoroughly combine pasta with sauce.
Mix together panko bread crumbs and 1 tablespoon melted butter in a small bowl.
Sprinkle mixture over macaroni and cheese. Sprinkle remaining 3/4 cup Cheddar cheese on top.
Bake in the preheated oven until top is golden brown, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: This panko mac and cheese is Chef John's easy-to-make, old-fashioned casserole with a crisp, buttery breadcrumb topping and a gooey, cheesy center.

video.description: Disregard your box of mac-n-cheese and learn how to make it from scratch. In this video, Chef John shows you how to bake his recipe for a gooey and cheesy macaroni and cheese dish. With a homemade cheese sauce made with three different types of cheese, pour it over a baking dish of cooked macaroni noodles. Top the macaroni with a panko breadcrumb and butter crust before baking in the oven. This easy homemade macaroni recipe is the perfect side for any dinner.

review.reviewBody: I made this for the boys before I went to work last night. I did not try this myself but based on the message I got at my break--they absolutely loved it. To be honest, there were no leftovers for me! They thought the crust was the best part. Note to self: double the crust ingredients next time.

Oh boy! I finally found the best macaroni and cheese I have ever had. I followed the recipe exactly, except I used only 12 oz. of macaroni, to make it more cheesy. It was a perfect ratio. I used 2% milk, and it worked great - creamy and satisfying. I don't know which I liked better, the crust or the filling, they were both delicious. You have to try this recipe! Thanks, Chef John!

Chef John I give you 5 stars for this one. The only ingredient I changed was to american cheese (more kid friendly)and I left out the salt because there was enough in the cheese. My kids could not get enough of it and it reheats very good. Thanks for sharing your recipe. Updated review: I have used this recipe for over 10 years now and its the most requested by my kids, their friends and family. So easy to make and just so darn good. They had me write out a recipe card for their family cook books and yes I gave the credit to Chef John.*****STILL AMAZING AFTER ALL THESE YEARS*****

Yes I love this recipe however I do use different cheeses. One of them is vintage Irish cheddar 7 ozs, 7ozs of sharp white, 8 ozs gruyere cheese, and 2 ozs smoked white cheddar cheese. Simply delightful and so easy to make.

Awesome! I did change a few things due to what I had on hand. Used 1c milk, 2c 1/2&1/2. 1c Gruyère, 2c cheddar. Didn’t have Dijon, did have sweet hot mustard. Used cheap shells ($.39/7oz x2), over salted the water just a bit, so didn’t add salt to sauce, shells added great flavor to wonderful sauce. Also doubled the panko. Cannot say enough how creamy it is and the shells added great texture with the perfect crunch on top!

Chef John recipes are a favorite in our family, and this one didn't disappoint. " good" is the highest rating at our house, and this earned it.

Followed the recipe but cut back on pasta a bit and added onion powder, garlic powder, and smoked paprika. I think a fine, aged cheddar freshly shredded helps. The nutmeg was great! I didn't have milk, so I subbed half heavy cream and half almond milk. Added a small bag of frozen broccoli at the last two minutes of boiling pasta, and added a large can (drained) of chicken breast while mixing it all together. Next time, I'll up the broccoli and chicken.

This is delicious. Used 14 ounces of rotini minus 1cup cooked, since that’s what I had on hand. Omitted spices, but used 1.5 cups sharp chedddar, 1.25 cups jack cheese and .25 cups of grated Parmesan. Really nice flavor with this blend. Used crushed saltines instead of panko on top and it worked well.

The sauce is divine! I cooked only 10 oz of macaroni as I like a lot of sauce to pasta ratio. Made as a child friendly option for a dinner however adults enjoyed this also. Combined everything except the topping in the morning and added the topping before cooking for supper.

I live in Georgia, so mac cheese is a big thing down here. One person said theirs was very dry. To prevent this, I would recommend putting the mac cheese under the broiler until it's golden brown on top, instead of baking it for 20 minutes. This should take less than 10 minutes and will allow the mac cheese to remain creamy, as it should be. I also suggest mixing up the cheese because straight cheddar is greasy. I usually use a mixture of 3 or 4 different kinds.

This was so good. Like Mac and Cheese for grown-ups. I halved the cheese sauce recipe for 5 ozs of uncooked elbows. Also used just good quality sharp cheddar. The panko didn't really brown enough in the oven for me so next time I'll just saute it in butter until browned before adding to the dish going into the oven. Love all of Chef John's recipes that I've tried so far.

Really good but the flavor was slightly off. Next time I won’t add the thyme at all and perhaps sub with garlic powder. The consistency was perfect. Video says to use 12oz for cheesier Mac. I increased the cheese sauce ingredients and stuck with 16oz. Use a large casserole so there is more room for the topping. I doubled the breadcrumb topping.
My entire family loves Mac N Cheese. This recipe is a great starter. I always add more spices to everything I make. But as always, I love Chef Johns recipes.
Delicious!
Great. Loved the topping. Will use that on every mac & cheese from now on! Not sure if the kids will go for all the spices. Will leave nutmeg out next time.
Easy nice size I hope as it is chef John's it is foolproof! A new recipe for me. There are so may choices but easy to make easy to digest.
We like our macaroni & cheese saucier. Next time, I'll reduce the noodles to 12 oz.
No changes to the recipe. I had to mix the Mac and sauce in the pan I cooked the Mac in then I added it to the 8x8. Flavor is very nice and this is a keeper.

This is the very best Mac and cheese. Follow the recipe but feel free to change up the cheese varieties. Different cheeses make a huge difference in flavors. Feel free to experiment. Thanks John for another wonderful recipe.

This Mac & cheese recipe was great! I accidentally used an entire stick of butter instead of 1/2, so I’m eager to make it with the correct amount- but the spices were lovely, perfect amount of cheese, definitely a new favorite.
Loved it
